newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - May 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Saturday her governemnt wanted to develop the hill tracts by utilising its natural resources and hoped of an early solution to the insurgency problem in the region.
Indian border security forces kidnapped four Bangladeshi nationals at a frontier area of eastern Sylhet district during the last couple of days.
Peace talks between the government and leaders of the tribal Shantibahini rebels begins in Dhaka on Sunday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina leaves Dhaka on Sunday for Maldives to attend the ninth summit of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) beginning in Male on Monday.
Communications Minister Anwar Hossain told the parliament on Saturday that the government was planning to introduce surcharge to raise funds for construction of road bridges.
A major change is likely in the board of councillors of the Dhaka Stock Exchange soon aimed at restoring investors' confidence in the capital market.
Bangladesh might have to import about 0.5 million tonnes of urea fertliser in the next fiscal year (1997-98) if domestic production capacity is not increased, government officials said.
Country's overall power situation improved on Saturday with generation reaching to 1,827 megawatt, highest in recent months, an official handout said. REUTER
